summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and Crescent Compute focused on reseller economics, private deployment interoperability, and a concrete lab benchmark plan. Crescent is evaluating reseller relationships for their channel push in EMEA and APAC and wants to validate performance on their staging hardware before committing to a go-to-market agreement.
meeting_header: Date: 2027-10-07 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~58m | Redwood: Liam, Priya, Aaron | Crescent: Sofia, Evan, Miles, Rhea
references: Partner program teaser (linked in chat) - redwood.com/partners/teaser (placeholder)
Security FAQ (Priya promised) - to be shared
Benchmark spreadsheet template - sample link referenced in discussion
transcript: [00:00] Liam: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. I'm Liam O'Connor from Redwood, AE on the partnerships team. Quick rundowns - Priya is our SE, Aaron on partnerships. Sofia, Evan, thanks for joining.
[00:22] Sofia: Hi Liam, thanks. We're excited. Crescent Compute does B2B GPU resale and we are looking for inference partners to bundle - need to understand interop and margins.
[00:45] Priya: Great. Quick ask from us: can you share the expected customer profiles and which regions you want to target? helps us recommend Dedicated vs Private models.
[01:10] Sofia: EMEA and APAC first, especially regulated customers in finance and healthcare. Typical ARR bands 50k-500k. We expect both managed hosted deals and some on-prem for big banks.
[01:38] Evan: technical note - a few prospects require in-country data residency and HSM integration for keys. We'll likely need Redwood Private or a VPC-onramp for those.
[02:05] Aaron: On the commercial side, we want clarity on partner margins, lead times for provisioning Dedicated pools, and co-sell support. Also do you have marketplace listings?
[02:31] Liam: Yup. We have a partner program with tiered margins, and there's a marketplace flow we can enable. Priya will share the margins deck and the private deployment checklist after the call.

[02:55] Miles: Quick tech question — drivers and runtime: Crescent customers run mixed quantized models and some custom kernels. How flexible is Redwood on kernel selection and driver versions in private deployments?

[03:20] Priya: Good question. For Private we surface kernel and runtime configuration per deployment. We try to maintain parity with hosted stacks but customers can pin kernels. Occasionally we see mismatched naming in our telemetry (K-V cache spelled out funny), so we'll validate with your engineers.
[03:50] Evan: We also need to know about SSO for partner ops and RBAC so our channel reps can get limited access. SSO via SAML?
[04:10] Liam: Yes SAML SSO and SCIM on enterprise tiers. We also support RBAC and audit logs — SOC2 controls are in our security FAQ. We'll push the FAQ and a SOC2 excerpt.
[04:35] Rhea: Commercial ops — what's typical time to onboard a reseller account and when would co-marketing kick in?

[04:50] Aaron: We usually have a 4-6 week pilot for a first proof-of-concept, then a formal reseller MSA. Co-marketing starts after we have an initial joint customer win or when both sides agree on GTM collateral.
[05:15] Sofia: For the 4-6 week pilot, do you require a staging cluster? Miles can host a staging environment on Crescent hardware for bench runs.
[05:35] Priya: That's ideal. If you provide access we can run a lab benchmark: latency/throughput across seq lengths and batching scenarios. We'll need model variants and tokenization specifics.
[06:00] Miles: We'll provide an A100 pool and a T4 mixed pool. Also need to coordinate network egress for telemetry—some clients lock down egress very tightly.

[06:20] Priya: We can support offline results export and encrypted artifact collection. For telemetry we have a minimal agent; if egress is blocked we can do an air-gapped run and transfer results securely.
[06:40] Evan: Any constraints about kernel signing or proprietary runtime blobs? Some customers want to run signed drivers only.
[06:55] Priya: We don't require unsigned drivers; customers can provide their signed drivers in Private deployments. We'll validate compatibility during benching.

[07:20] Liam: On margins — we feel flexible early in the partnership, but need a baseline: typical channel margin tiers are 15/20/30 depending on volume and go-to-market contribution. We'll share specifics.
[07:45] Rhea: Do you offer deal registration/incentives so our reps don't get undercut?
[07:58] Aaron: Yes, we support deal registration and partner-assigned quotas. We can map an escalation path if a direct sales motion overlaps.
[08:15] Sofia: A few prospects asked about audit logs and KMS integration for customer-owned keys — can Redwood integrate with external KMS/HSM?
[08:30] Priya: Yes — KMS integrations are supported in Private and Dedicated with customer-managed keys. HSM integrations are possible but need an architecture review.
[08:50] Miles: For the bench runs, do you have a preferred load profile? our customers range from low latency chat to high-throughput batch embedding jobs.

[09:10] Priya: We'll propose two profiles: conversational low-latency (seq 64/128) with strict 99th p95 goals, and throughput embedding jobs (batch sizes variable). We'll include continuous batching knobs and cache warmup guidance.
[09:40] Evan: Does Redwood offer automatic fallback between hosted and dedicated models if capacity spikes? Some clients need graceful degradation policies.
[09:58] Liam: Yes, routing policies can fallback to compatible model variants or different capacity tiers. We'll document recommended fallback policies for your sales plays.
[10:18] Sofia: On the legal side, what does the reseller agreement look like re: liability and data residency? our legal team will want to review quickly.

[10:35] Liam: We'll share a draft MSA and reseller exhibit. Standard clauses, plus options for data residency commitments. Legal can loop in from our side after you share your standard CLA or partner terms.
[10:55] Rhea: Do you have examples of co-sell plays with other resellers?
[11:05] Aaron: Yes — we'll include case studies in the deck. One recent channel partner had a 3x expansion after a pilot show of latency improvements and integrated billing.
[11:28] Sofia: Great. Technical: how do you handle KV cache and model version pinning — customers want deterministic responses for regulated use cases.
[11:45] Priya: We expose KV cache controls and you can pin exact model versions and quantization profiles. We also support eval sets to detect regressions when changing model versions.
[12:07] Miles: Any constraints on custom ops and compiled kernels for LLM inference? we sometimes need fused kernels for perf.

[12:28] Priya: Custom ops are possible in Private with an integration window. We typically ask for a performance and security review; fused kernels require testing in our harness and signed binaries for production.
[12:50] Evan: On monitoring — what's in the Redwood Console for partners? can we white-label or share dashboards with customers?

[13:10] Liam: Console has per-route latency/cost, token-level breakdowns, and tracing hooks. For partners, we can enable dedicated views or export dashboards; white-labeling is limited but we can provide embeddable widgets.
[13:40] Sofia: About pricing: is pricing based purely on tokens or do you have reserved capacity pricing for Dedicated pools we can resell?
[13:58] Aaron: We have usage pricing for hosted plus reserved capacity for Dedicated. Reseller economics can be structured on markup over reserved unit costs or revenue share — we'll propose options.
[14:22] Miles: Network egress costs: if Crescent handles customers, will we be on the hook for egress or does your model allow pass-through?
[14:40] Liam: We can do flexible billing. For Dedicated/Private, egress and infra costs are typically handled by the customer or partner depending on the contract.
[15:05] Rhea: Quick nit — provisioning times for Dedicated GPU pools? Some vendors quote 6-8 weeks.
[15:18] Priya: Typical is 3-6 weeks if capacity available. For on-prem/hybrid it's tied to Crescent provisioning schedules.
[15:35] Evan: Any limitations on model sizes? we deal with 30B to 70B models mostly.
[15:50] Priya: We support up to LLMs in that range; memory and KV cache behavior changes with longer context. We'll run a memory/latency projection during bench runs.
[16:10] Sofia: Are there any feature flags partners get earlier? We're curious about early access to Optimize tooling.
[16:28] Liam: Yes, strategic partners get early trial for Redwood Optimize and suggestions for batching/quantization. We'll include that in partnership tiers.
[16:45] Miles: We'll provision staging and share creds — note we sometimes obfuscate names in telemetry for privacy, so there may be mismatch in logs.
[17:00] Priya: Noted. We'll accept obfuscated IDs and map them during analysis. If needed we can run tests with synthetic payloads too.
[17:25] Evan: On integration, will we need an agent inside the customer's VPC or do you prefer API-only?
[17:40] Priya: Both are supported. For low-latency on-prem, an agent + private control plane is recommended; for hosted, API-only is common.
[17:58] Sofia: Let's talk go-to-market: Crescent wants joint sales decks and a demo kit. Can Redwood support a partner demo with a canned dataset for finance use cases?
[18:15] Aaron: Absolutely. We'll assemble a demo kit and a runbook for partners including playbooks for demo scripts and sample prompts.
[18:34] Rhea: About support — what are the SLAs and escalation contacts for partner-facing tickets?
[18:47] Liam: Partners on tier 2+ get direct SE support and a named CSM; SLAs vary by tier but we'll include a matrix in the deck.
[19:05] Miles: Can we do a short POC where Redwood runs inference against our customer dataset with PII redaction?
[19:20] Priya: We can, but we'll need a DPA and a data handling agreement. We can also run synthetic PII-masked datasets if faster.
[19:40] Evan: Any gotchas around licensing models for open models you host? open-source license compliance is important to some customers.
[19:58] Priya: We maintain a model catalog with licensing metadata and can flag models with restrictive licenses; we'll share the catalog excerpt.
[20:20] Sofia: Good. For the bench, can Redwood provide a short pre-bench questionnaire so Miles can prep the nodes?
[20:38] Priya: Yes — we'll send a bench prep form (GPU type, driver versions, kernel versions, allowed egress, test models, tokenization).
[20:55] Liam: I'll follow up with the partner deck and commercial template. Priya will send the bench prep file and security FAQ. Aaron will be the primary channel contact.
[21:15] Sofia: Sounds good. Any immediate blocker from our side? I think we need the deck and the bench windows.
[21:30] Rhea: Also legal needs the reseller terms before we present to our legal team in two weeks.
[21:45] Liam: We'll aim to send the MSA draft and reseller exhibit with margins in three business days.
[22:05] Evan: One last technical clar — can fallback between models maintain session continuity or does it reset KV cache?
[22:25] Priya: If fallback is to a compatible variant with shared vocab and KV format, continuity can be preserved, otherwise a cache reset may be needed. We'll note this in the bench run.
[22:50] Miles: Okay we'll prepare staging access and a set of representative prompts and models.
[23:10] Liam: Great. Thanks everyone — we'll reconvene after we circulate materials. Proposed next call after bench is complete in ~2 weeks.
[23:30] Sofia: Thanks — appreciate the thoroughness. Bye all.
[23:40] Aaron: Thanks, bye.
[23:45] Priya: Bye.
[23:50] (call ends)
[24:00] Transcript notes: occasional transcription artifacts — 'K-V cash' appears in raw ASR, and some proper nouns (kernel builds) were misrecognized.
